Esteban Ocon Denies Physical Altercation Claims Following Haas F1 Team Departure

01 Nov 2026, 06:05 PM IST · GlobeWire Daily Sports Desk · Source: www.bbc.co.uk

2 min read

Key takeawaysEsteban Ocon has publicly denied recent media reports alleging that his abrupt departure from the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend was the result of a physical confrontation with Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

Ocon Responds to Media Reports

Esteban Ocon has publicly denied recent media reports alleging that his abrupt departure from the Mexico City Grand Prix weekend was the result of a physical confrontation with Haas team principal Ayao Komatsu.

The 30-year-old French driver released a statement on social media addressing the claims. While Ocon acknowledged that "a difference in viewpoints led to a discussion with the parties involved," he stated that he "categorically rejected any reports or allegations suggesting that any form of physical violence was used to resolve any differences of any nature."

Ocon's statement was issued following a report by French publication *L'Equipe*, which claimed that a meeting between the driver and Komatsu "ended abruptly, perhaps even physically."

Context of the Team Decision

The decision by Haas to stand Ocon down for the remainder of the Mexico weekend followed an on-track dispute during the second practice session on Friday.

  • The Tyre Dispute: Race engineer Laura Mueller informed Ocon that the team's plan to run soft-compound tyres had changed in favor of the medium compound.
  • The Driver Response: Ocon radioed back, stating: "No, no. I want to do soft... don't do that to me, come on."

Following the practice session, Haas announced that Ocon would be replaced for the weekend's race by Hirakawa, though the team has not issued further details regarding the specifics of the post-session discussions.

Future Implications and Unknowns

Beyond the current Grand Prix weekend, several key details remain unconfirmed:

  • Future Races: Neither Haas nor Ocon's management team have commented on whether the driver will return to the cockpit for any of the remaining races this season. It was previously announced last month that Ocon is set to leave Haas at the end of the 2025 season to be replaced by Formula 2 championship leader Rafael Camara.
  • Official Team Position: Haas has only officially confirmed Ocon's removal for the Mexico City event.

In his statement, Ocon urged observers to avoid speculation. "I strongly condemn violence in all its forms and firmly believe that disagreements should always be handled with professionalism, respect, and mutual understanding," he said. "Further updates will be communicated in due course."

How to Verify

Readers seeking verified updates on the situation can monitor official announcements directly through the official Formula 1 website or the official communication channels of the Haas F1 Team.
